data.gender_notes: Krishnadasa is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Krishnadasa is a combination of two words: Krishna and dasa. Krishna means 'God' and dasa means 'servant'. Thus, Krishnadasa can be interpreted as 'God's servant' or 'devotee of Krishna'. The name Krishnadasa carries the meaning “God's servant” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Krishnadasa usually hope their child will grow to embody god's servant and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A name that signifies devotion and surrender to the divine.
data.etymology: Krishnadasa belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “God's servant.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Krishnadasa total 6, giving a life-path number of 6. Number 6 is linked with Venus and with the qualities of responsibility, care and community.

data.cultural_impact: The name Krishnadasa holds great significance in the Indian subcontinent where Krishna is a beloved deity. The name is a testament to the devotional tradition in Hinduism, where one's identity is often linked to their relationship with a particular deity. Krishnadasa is also a common name among the Vaishnavas, a sect of Hinduism that is devoted to Krishna.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Krishnadasa reflects a person's spiritual bond and devotion towards Krishna. It signifies the surrendering of oneself to the divine will of Krishna and striving to live a life in devotion and service to him. The name serves as a constant reminder of one's spiritual goals and the importance of staying connected to the deity.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Krishnadasa: Devoted servant of Lord Krishna. Symbolizes an unwavering devotion and surrender to the divine will of Krishna. Spiritually, it represents a life dedicated to the pursuit of love and service to the divine.

historical_references.reference: Krishnadasa I, also known as Krishna Deva Raya, was a powerful ruler of the Vijayanagara Empire from 1509 to 1529 CE. He is considered one of the greatest monarchs in Indian history for his military conquests, patronage of art, literature and temple construction.

Krishnadasa Mutha, a 17th-century Maratha warrior and commander who served under the Maratha king Shivaji Raje Bhonsle. He is best known for his role in the Battle of Pratapgarh (1659 CE) where he successfully defended the Maratha stronghold against the Mughal forces led by Shah Jahan.

modern_usage.modern_context: The name 'Krishnadasa' is derived from Hindu mythology, specifically the name of the deity Lord Krishna and the title 'das', meaning servant or devotee. In modern context, this name is most commonly associated with the renowned 16th-century Carnatic music composer and musician, Tyagaraja, who adopted the name 'Krishnadasa' as a mark of his devotion to Lord Krishna. Krishnadasa's compositions continue to be popular and are celebrated worldwide, with modern audiences accessing them through various digital platforms such as YouTube, Spotify, and Apple Music. These platforms have enabled the widespread dissemination and accessibility of Krishnadasa's music, allowing it to reach a global audience and continue to be a source of inspiration and cultural heritage.
